title: Lesson 85: General systems architecture: the architecture of an AI platform, end-to-end walkthrough
description: Checks that you can name the layers of an AI platform, trace a request through the trust boundaries of a multi-agent design, decide which model work is priced per token, and choose the controls that limit what a successful prompt injection can achieve.

questions.question: An orchestrator is manipulated by a poisoned knowledge article and forwards its context to three specialists. Which control does the lesson's trust guidance prescribe at the receiving end?
options: Lower the model temperature for specialist calls
Treat inter-agent message content with the same scrutiny as external user input
Log the specialist output for monthly review
Route the request to a larger model
questions.explanation: Trust propagates through a multi-agent chain, so an orchestrator that has been manipulated passes the problem to every specialist that receives its context. The guidance is that each agent validates the context it receives before acting, because trust in the caller's identity does not mean trust in the caller's content. Logging after the fact and changing model size address output quality rather than the injection path.

questions.question: In the service desk worked example, which part of the design keeps the assistant from sending a customer response without a person involved?
options: No send, no close, no entitlement change.
questions.explanation: The tools row of the design allows reading the case, reading entitlement, creating a task and drafting a response, while the platform keeps the send, close and entitlement change capabilities out of the allowlist. Task creation is reversible and logged, which is why it is permitted. The other options are capabilities the design does grant, not limits on what the agent can do.

questions.question: A client asks which single control most reduces the damage a successful prompt injection could do. Which control does the lesson name as the highest-value one for exactly that reason?
questions.explanation: The lesson calls least privilege for tools the single highest-value control because each tool runs under a permission set sized to the action, which caps what a successful injection can achieve. A stop path limits how long an agent runs rather than what it is allowed to touch. Evaluation sets and traces detect and explain regressions, and both depend on the permission boundary being right.
